html:
A battle on 8 September 1380 at Kulikovo Field, near the upper Don south of Moscow, in which Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeated Mamai, the warlord who held power in the western Golden Horde. It was the first big victory of the Russian princes over the Horde, and it earned Dmitry the name Donskoy, "of the Don".

The Horde was then split by two decades of civil war, and Mamai, who was not of Genghis Khan's line, ruled through puppet khans. Moscow had stopped paying him tribute. Mamai's ally, Jogaila of Lithuania, arrived too late to fight. Both sides lost heavily.

The victory did not end Mongol rule. Two years later the khan Tokhtamysh, who had since overthrown Mamai, burned Moscow, and Dmitry paid tribute again. Russia only threw off the Horde a century later, after the stand on the Ugra in 1480. But Kulikovo showed that the Grand Duchy of Moscow could lead the Russian princes against the Horde, and later writers made it the birth of the Russian nation. The monk Sergius of Radonezh is said to have blessed Dmitry before the battle.
